desc: The seed note has a topic-label front — 'In system design, what is gRPC?' — whose back bundles three independently recallable facts into one answer: gRPC is an RPC framework, it serializes with Protocol Buffers, and it runs over HTTP/2. A card like this tests recognition, not recall: on review, half-recalling one of the three facts is easy to mistake for mastering the card. The agent should split the note so each fact gets its own card with a front that cues exactly it — the framework identity, the serialization format, and the transport protocol — preserving every fact from the original back. The seed is otherwise clean (house-style prefix, no formatting defects), so the split is the only change required.

notes.front: In system design, what is gRPC?
notes.back: High-performance RPC framework using binary Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2

judge_assertions: After applying the change set, the three facts bundled in the seed's back — that gRPC is an RPC framework, that it serializes with Protocol Buffers, and that it runs over HTTP/2 — are tested on separate cards: a card whose front asks what gRPC is and whose back gives only its identity as an RPC framework, a card for the serialization format (Protocol Buffers), and a card for the transport protocol (HTTP/2).

After applying the change set, every card in the cluster tests exactly one of the three facts: no card's front bundles two or more of them into one question, and no card's back chains two or more of them in one answer.
